source.title: Ballymena Observer, 9 June 1939, p. 10 ("Rural Council and Guardians: annual meetings held; chairmen re-elected"); Ballymena Weekly Telegraph, 6 May 1939, p. 2 ("R.D.C. elections: retiring members unopposed"); Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1933, p. 10 ("Ballymena Rural Council: no contest"); Ballymena Observer, 16 June 1939, p. 2 ("Ballymena Guardians")
source.publisher: Ballymena Observer (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: no contest in the division (Ballymena Weekly Telegraph, 6 May 1939, p. 2); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Ballymena Observer, 9 June 1939, p. 10: 'On the motion of Mr. M'Millen, seconded by Mr. Carson, Mr. Chesney was again re-elected chairman'; Ballymena Observer, 16 June 1939, p. 2: 'Samuel M'Millen' present)

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 1 June 1939. There was no change in personnel and no contest: the retiring member was the only nominee in twelve divisions and no nominations were received in the other eleven. Poll date Thursday 1 June 1939 (Ballymena Observer 2 Jun 1939 p. 5; BNL 4 May 1939 p. 13); filed under 1939-06-01, renamed from 1939-05-31 (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Ballyclug, Dunminning, Glenravel, Kells, Kirkinriola, Longmore, Toome and Tullygarley. division inferred from the 1 June 1933 return (Samuel M'Millen; Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1933, p. 10); the Ballymena Observer, 9 June 1939, p. 10 names the member as sitting for the new council (annual (first) meeting of the new Ballymena Rural Council, Wednesday 7 June 1939: members present, chairman, co-options, committees). The 1933 nomination report as transcribed gives 'Samuel M'Mullan'; the meeting reports print 'Samuel M'Millen'. Returned unopposed.
